text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller criticises speculation of a military coup and says no solutions exist outside democracy.
- New government searches in parliament depend on whether an estimated 10 deputies will leave the conservative junior coalition party, which is in an alliance with the Islamists.
- Leftist opposition leader Bulent Ecevit says that there is a risk of a coup, not by the army but by the ruling Islamist Welfare.
- The lawyer of late mobster Abdulah Catli says the gangster was recruited for shady state busineess by late President Turgut Ozal.
- The Islamist mayor to Sincan in Ankara -- suspended from his duties after holding an anti-Israeli protest in his district -- was questioned by Ankara's state security court.
- The second hearing of forty-eight policemen charged for the killing of leftist journalist Metin Goktepe in police custody will be held in the town of Afyon.
- New regulations are being prepared for tax debtors.
- The foreign minister, Tansu Ciller, escaped a new corruption charge after a renewed parliamentary vote rejected setting up an investigation against her.
